#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE:
#   Slurm uses a job array with concurrency limit (--array 3203-4002%30).
#   Flux job arrays are not available as a universally portable batch-script directive.
#
# Run with:
#   flux batch <this_script> -- <TASK_ID>

# Slurm resources:
#   -G 1
#   --exclude=ice[...]
#   -t 0-05:00
#   --array 3203-4002%30
#   --mem 16G
#   --chdir=/home/jrick6/repos/data
#   --job-name=gen_image_var
#   --output=.../%x.%A.%a.out

#flux: --job-name=gen_image_var
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: --time-limit=5h

# Omitted Slurm option: -G 1 (GPU request)
# Flux GPU requests are site/config dependent (often via custom resource types).
# Performance implication: job may start without a GPU, causing failure or severe slowdown.

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem 16G
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on a node with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm options: --array 3203-4002%30
# Flux job arrays (and concurrency limits) are not available as a universally portable batch-script directive.
# Performance implication: you must submit many jobs manually and manage throttling externally; this can increase scheduler overhead and reduce throughput.

# Omitted Slurm option: --exclude=ice[...]
# Flux node exclusion is site/config dependent; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run on excluded/problematic nodes, impacting reliability/performance.

# Omitted Slurm option: --output with %x/%A/%a tokens
# Slurm token expansion is not portable in Flux output directives.
# Performance implication: none, but log naming/uniqueness may differ.

# Slurm --chdir: emulate by cd.
cd /home/jrick6/repos/data

TASK_ID=${1:-3203}

echo "Running on host: $(hostname)"

nvidia-smi

/home/jrick6/.conda/envs/simclr/bin/python generate_image_variations.py \
  -tfp "/home/jrick6/tensorflow_datasets/imagenet2012_subset_id/1pct/5.0.0/imagenet2012_subset-train.tfrecord-00004-of-00016" \
  -o "/home/jrick6/tensorflow_datasets/imagenet2012_subset_id_variations0/1pct/5.0.0/dir_imagenet2012_subset-train.tfrecord-00004-of-00016/imagenet2012_subset-train.tfrecord-00004-of-00016" \
  --input_id "$TASK_ID"

reasons: The original Slurm job required 1 GPU (`-G 1`) but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this may allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run much slower.

The original Slurm job requested 16G of memory (`--mem 16G`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this may under-provision the job and risk OOM.

The original Slurm job used an array with a concurrency limit (`--array 3203-4002%30`) but the Flux resource section does not provide an equivalent array/throttling mechanism; this changes the intended number of scheduled job instances and throughput.
